name: k-switch
description: Roadmap #10: the k-switch, executed — order superposition over k! topological sorts (k=3, six orders), the machine-verified layer of the N-switch query separation. Known in theory (ARA14: O(n) vs O(n²) queries), never machine-verified. Delivered here: the 3-switch as an executable isometry with certificate; the commuting-vs-anticommuting promise read out deterministically via the exact parity-orthogonality law (control ends in the uniform state vs the permutation-parity state, inner product exactly 0 — dimension-free, weaker than ARA14's d>=N! full problem); structural blindness of plain fixed orders (every order's output is the input up to a global phase, trace distance exactly 0 across the whole promise class); and the three-stage scheduling contact surface (six-order switch vs six fixed orders on an alloc-alloc-exec chain)
